title: New-Onset Congestive Heart Failure
scenario: A 72-year-old male with hypertension and type 2 diabetes presents to the emergency department with progressive shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling of both ankles over the past week. He has no prior cardiac history.

lines: 72-year-old male presents with 1 week of worsening exertional dyspnea, orthopnea (using 3 pillows), and bilateral ankle edema. Denies chest pain. Bibasilar crackles auscultated. Fine pitting edema to mid-shin bilaterally. Appears anxious and short of breath while speaking. Alert and oriented x3. No prior diagnosis of heart failure.
IV access established. 12-lead ECG, chest x-ray, and labs ordered. Oxygen 3L started per nasal cannula. Client placed in high Fowler's position. Cardiac monitor applied showing sinus tachycardia.
Echocardiogram results reviewed with provider: ejection fraction 35%. New diagnosis of congestive heart failure documented. IV furosemide administered per order.
Client reports breathing is much easier. Crackles diminished at the bases. Voided 850 mL clear yellow urine since diuretic. Sitting up comfortably, no longer using accessory muscles.
Insert indwelling urinary catheter, monitor strict intake and output
2 gram sodium diet, 1.5 L fluid restriction
Continuous cardiac monitoring and pulse oximetry
Notify provider for urine output < 30 mL/hr

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which 4 findings on admission require immediate follow-up?
children.rationale: Crackles, hypoxia, tachypnea, and orthopnea all reflect pulmonary congestion from new-onset heart failure and demand prompt intervention. Normal mentation, temperature, and potassium do not.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it reflects left-sided heart failure, right-sided heart failure, or both. Each finding may reflect more than one.
children.rationale: Pulmonary congestion (crackles, orthopnea) is a hallmark of left-sided failure; systemic congestion (peripheral edema) reflects right-sided failure. BNP is elevated with either type.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the client's priority problem is {1}, and the priority nursing goal is to {2}.

choices.text: impaired gas exchange from pulmonary congestion

children.rationale: Hypoxia and crackles make impaired gas exchange the most immediate life threat, so improving oxygenation is the priority goal over the other valid but less urgent problems.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client.

rows.text: Restrict fluids to 1.5 L per day
Administer a 500 mL normal saline bolus

children.rationale: Diuresis, upright positioning, and fluid restriction relieve volume overload. A saline bolus and high sodium add fluid and worsen congestion, so both are contraindicated.

children.subject: Pharmacology
children.stem: After administering IV furosemide, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
children.rationale: Loop diuretics cause potassium loss, diuresis, and possible hypotension, so the nurse tracks electrolytes, output, weight, and blood pressure. Total fluid withholding and holding the prescribed ACE inhibitor are not indicated.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which findings indicate the treatment has been effective? Select all that apply.
children.rationale: Improved respiratory rate, oxygenation, breath sounds, and brisk diuresis show the fluid overload is resolving. Rising heart rate and blood pressure would signal worsening, not improvement.
